title: Can You Trust Your Trust Measure?
base_benchmarks: Reliance Intention Scale by Lyons & Guznov (RIS)
The Trust Perception Scale-HRI by Schaefer (TPS-HRI)
The Multidimensional Measure of Trust by Ullman & Malle (MDMT)
Scale of Trust in Automated Systems (TAS)
findings: This paper does not contain any findings related to religion. Its key findings are that people's mental models of robots are fragile and context-dependent, which affects whether they find certain trust questionnaire items (especially those with anthropomorphic traits like 'principled' or 'benevolent') applicable. The study also found that while overall trust scores remained robust even when participants were forced to rate items they found non-applicable, the interpretation of these scores could be flawed due to the 'mental gymnastics' people perform to answer them.

measurement_description: The paper does not measure anything related to faith or religion. It investigates the applicability of different human-robot interaction (HRI) trust questionnaires to various robots and interaction scenarios.
